TRM Labs, an American blockchain analysis firm, reveals that North Korea's Bureau 121 was responsible for a $6.3 billion theft on cryptocurrency exchange Binance, the largest heist in history, prompting an investigation by the FBI and the US Secret Service.
The Trump administration authorizes the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine.


=== November ===

November 1
Democratic senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut is hospitalized after suffering a stroke.
A Learjet 60 crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board.
Democratic representative Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers over Democratic Abdul Al-Sayed in the Senate election in Michigan. Al-Sayed had previously defeated Stevens in the primaries. In response, Stevens's staff members resign and the Michigan Democratic Party revokes Stevens's party membership.
November 2
Small-scale, "defensive" strikes are carried out by the US against Iranian positions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
A Washington state resident dies of bird flu.

November 3
2026 United States midterm elections: in a blue wave, the Democratic Party wins majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.
Trump announces that the US will terminate all military aid to Israel, totaling $4 billion per year, by the end of 2026, but will continue to sell military hardware.
November 4
First Lady Melania Trump receives the Order of Princess Olga from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for her significant personal contribution to humanitarian relief efforts in Ukraine.
The US imposes new sanctions on companies and individuals in India and Turkey with ties to the Iranian government.
A mass shooting occurs at a Citibank building. Two people were killed including the perpetrator.
November 5
Harmeet Dhillon, the head of the Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division, resigns following the midterm elections.
A Venezuelan man is detained near the White House on suspicion of plotting to assassinate Trump.
Governor of California Gavin Newsom announces plans to commute the death sentences of all 548 prisoners on the state's death row to life imprisonment without parole, in what would be the largest mass commutation of death sentences in U.S. history. The move requires approval from the California Supreme Court for 382 of the prisoners.
November 6
The number of measles cases in the United States exceeds 5,000 for the first time since 1991.
Susie Wiles, Trump's White House Chief of Staff, is replaced by Stephen Miller, her deputy.
Eight Canadian money services companies are sanctioned by the U.S. for dealing with the Iranian government.
The US cuts off money exchanger MEXC due to transactions involving Iran, North Korea, and Russia.
Thomas Markle, the father of Megan, Duchess of Sussex, is detained in Lakeland, Florida, for allegedly possessing sex abuse photographs of preadolescent girls, including images depicting himself with them.
Trump declares that the US conducted "minor" strikes against Iran, targeting "a little bit of an anti-aircraft device."
The Central Command (CENTCOM) announces a $20 million incentive "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear program.
November 7 – CENTCOM expands its interdiction efforts against the Iranian government beyond its existing naval blockade by establishing Task Force Iron Gate to obstruct "illicit" shipments and weapons transit across land borders and the Caspian Sea.
November 8 – Nvidia launches an investigation into allegations that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was targeted by Chinese intelligence, following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
November 9 – The U.S. evacuates its military aircraft from RAF Mildenhall following a reported threat from Iran.
November 10
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is relocated from his Washington, DC house to a military base due to threats against his life related to Operation Economic Outcast against the Iranian government.
The House of Representatives blocks an impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth initiated by outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) by a vote of 211–204. The vote is along party lines with the exception of Massie, and eleven Democrats are no-shows for the vote.
House Republicans elect Rep. Jim Jordan (R-OH) as their minority leader for the next Congress, succeeding outgoing Speaker of the House Mike Johnson. Jordan defeats Rep. Steve Scalise (R-LA) by 106–73 votes in a secret ballot.

November 11
A three-story apartment building collapses in Brooklyn, New York City, killing eight people and injuring 17 others.
A car crashes into a food stand near a bus stop in the North Hollywood section of Los Angeles, killing three people and seriously injuring three more.
Democrat Scott Colom defeats incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi Senate election, becoming the state's first black U.S. senator since 1874 and the first Democrat elected to the seat since 1982.
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth awards a medal to a war memorial guard who reprimanded him.
The SS United States, once the flagship ocean liner of United States Lines and holder of the Blue Riband, is sunk off the coast of Destin, Florida to become the world's largest artificial reef.
November 12
Jensen Huang resigns as the CEO of Nvidia, following revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China.
One person is killed and four are injured in a gun attack at and outside a fitness center in downtown Washington, D.C.
Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) challenges Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY) for majority leader in the upcoming Congress. Van Hollen represents the progressive wing of the Democratic Party.
2026 Microsoft outage: a global outage disrupts Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and Copilot, affecting businesses and government agencies worldwide for two days.

November 13
The FBI announces that North Korea used fake video calls to steal $400 million in cryptocurrency.
The International Criminal Court closes its investigations into suspected war crimes committed by US troops in Afghanistan, following institutional sanctions imposed by the US on the court.
The FAA issues a nationwide ground stop for the first time since 9/11, due to a "telecommunications outage".
2026 New Orleans ship collision: An oil tanker collides with the docked river boat American Heritage in New Orleans, Louisiana, injuring 32 people.
A bomb is found at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, after a "credible bomb threat" was called in. An evacuation is ordered for residents within a one-mile radius of the site, and some local events are cancelled.
The United States officially loses its measles elimination status.
November 14 – After a 22-hour orbital test flight, SpaceX successfully recovers its Starship vehicle with mechanical launch-tower arms at Starbase in Texas, marking the first-ever recovery of an orbital upper-stage spacecraft.
November 16 – US intelligence detects potential Iranian plans for dirty bomb or chemical attacks against senior Trump administration officials in Washington, D.C, an allegation dismissed by Iran.
November 16–17:
November 2026 technology outages: after the global Microsoft outage and the nationwide FAA ground stop, more technology outages occur in the United States. Several major U.S. national banks and financial services companies (including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and U.S. Bank) also experience service disruptions and outages beginning on November 16. Most of the banks' issues stem from disruptions to JPMorgan Chase systems. The National Security Agency's internal communications network experiences an outage on November 17. Apple also experiences an outage with several of its products and services on November 17.
November 17
The U.S. military states that in response to an earlier Iranian drone attack that targeted a US radar installation at Isa Air Base in Bahrain, US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
A federal judge in Brooklyn sentences Pakistani national Asif Merchant to 27½ years imprisonment for plotting with the Iranian government to assassinate U.S. officials, including Trump, Biden, and Nikki Haley.
Trump meets with the leaders of Australia, India, and Japan in Manila, Philippines, for the first Quadrilateral Security Dialogue summit of his second term, announcing multilateral agreements to secure critical mineral supply chains.
Democrat Mary Peltola defeats incumbent Republican senator Dan Sullivan in the 2026 United States Senate election in Alaska, becoming the first Alaska Native elected to the United States Senate and the first Democrat to win a Senate election in the state since 2008.
November 18 – NASA's Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object to reach a distance of one light-day (25.9 billion kilometres) from Earth, nearly 50 years after its launch in 1977. At this distance, radio signals take 24 hours to travel between Earth and the spacecraft.
November 19
During the 2026 APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, Trump, Chinese president Xi Jinping, and Russian president Vladimir Putin hold their first-ever trilateral meeting and release a joint statement on energy supplies, nuclear non-proliferation, and UN reform.
San Francisco-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic, developer of the Claude chatbot, makes its debut on the Nasdaq following an $81.3 billion initial public offering, the largest in history. The offering values the company at approximately $1.5 trillion, surpassing the previous IPO fundraising record set by SpaceX earlier in the year.
Following widespread technological outages across the country, Trump removes National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross and appoints Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies as acting director.
The FCC bans Chinese firms from direct access to United States phone numbers in bid to curb robocalls.
November 20
The US Treasury sanctions "trustees" who receive oil revenues for the Iranian government, adding that in many cases they have kept the funds for personal gain.
The Nasdaq Composite falls 5.28% amid a widespread sell-off in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks, ending the week down 10% in one of its steepest weekly declines since March 2020. The S&P 500 also falls 3.7%, entering correction territory.
A federal jury in Los Angeles convicts Jonathan Rinderknecht on two charges relating to the Palisades Fire of January 2025, which killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 structures. The fire was one of the most destructive in California's history.


== Predicted and scheduled events ==


=== November ===
November 20 – The United States Army plans to detonate a 10,000 pound pile of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown (near Burlington). The detonation has the potential to produce a major plume of lead-contaminated smoke, which would effect Eastern Iowa, Western Illinois, as well as the entire Mississippi River going southward.


=== December ===
December 3 – Nidal Hasan is scheduled to be executed. If carried out, he would be the first sitting member of the United States Armed Forces to be executed since John A. Bennett was executed in 1961 for rape and attempted murder.

== References ==

Teófimo López vs. Shakur Stevenson, billed as The Ring 6, was a Junior welterweight professional boxing match contested between The Ring and WBO junior welterweight champion Teofimo Lopez, and WBC lightweight champion Shakur Stevenson. The bout took place on January 31, 2026, at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Stevenson won by unanimous decision.


== Background ==
On December 1, 2025, It was officially announced Teofimo Lopez will defend his The Ring and WBO junior Welterweight Championship titles against WBC lightweight champion Shakur Stevenson.
After Lopez lost his unified lightweight titles to George Kambosos Jr. in November 2021, he moved up to junior welterweight and won the WBO and The Ring titles in June 2023 with a unanimous decision victory over Josh Taylor. He made two title defenses in 2024 before defeating the previously unbeaten Arnold Barboza Jr. in New York City in May 2025.
Going into the bout, Stevenson was a three-division world champion, having previously held titles at featherweight and super featherweight before winning the WBC lightweight title in November 2023.


== The fight ==
Lopez struggled against Stevenson's boxing ability and jab, and Stevenson appeared dominant throughout the fight and bloodied Lopez, holding a 165 to 72 advantage in punches landed. The three official scorecards had Stevenson winning 119–109.


== Aftermath ==
In April 2026, Lopez discussed the fight and accused Stevenson of using tactics that were beyond standard exchanges, particularly at close range. He said Stevenson stood on his feet, used his elbows during clinches, and described these as part of a "dirty fight" strategy, which affected the flow of the fight. Lopez stated that these moments disrupted his rhythm and limited his offensive opportunities.
